title: Product model
description: The source of truth for every later stage. Nothing may appear in a video that is not traceable to this document, and nothing enters this document without a source reference.

surface_type.description: How the product is actually experienced. Drives which inspection adapter and which capture adapter run. `mixed` requires primary_surface.

primary_surface.description: Required when surface_type is `mixed`: the one surface the video will actually show.

one_line.description: What it does, in the project's own terms. No positioning yet.

primary_user.description: Who this is for, specifically. 'developers' is too broad to direct a video.

problem.description: The problem in the user's world, not the feature's absence.

mechanism.description: How it actually works. Concrete enough that a viewer could picture it.

proof.description: Every claim the video is allowed to make, each with the evidence that supports it. A claim with no source cannot be shown.

visual_surfaces.description: What can actually be put on screen. For a CLI the terminal is a visual surface, not supporting material.

forbidden_claims.description: Things that are true-adjacent but unsupported, or that the maintainer does not want said. Enforced by substring match at review time.

verbatim_copy.description: Strings that must appear exactly as written, each traceable to a file. This is what makes the video's copy checkable rather than plausible.

identity.description: The project's own visual identity, extracted rather than invented.

logo_usable_on_dark.description: False when the mark is dark-on-transparent and would vanish on a dark ground. Recorded so the director does not discover it at render time.

recent_commits.description: Real history. Usable on screen for products whose story is the work itself.

signals.description: What the deterministic scan found. Written by the CLI, not the model; present so classification is auditable.

source.description: Where a fact came from. Byte offsets make the fidelity check exact rather than fuzzy.

strength.description: measured: a number produced by a real run. demonstrated: the product visibly doing it. documented: the project states it. inferred: true but not stated — the weakest thing a video may show, and never as a headline.

shows_well.description: Whether this proof can carry a scene on its own.

capture.description: How this surface will be recorded. `synthesized` means brag will build it from real strings rather than record it.

whitespace_significant.description: True when the exact spacing matters — aligned CLI output, indented trees, code. The compiler must not normalise it.
